tEn: Leaked Anthropic Draft AI Regulatory Bill Is Unacceptable and Troubling
tZh: 泄露的 Anthropic 人工智能监管法案草案不可接受且令人不安
sEn: A leaked Anthropic draft AI regulatory bill is unacceptable and troubling because it trades broad preemption for modest regulatory gains and weakens key safety provisions.
sZh: 泄露的 Anthropic 人工智能监管法案草案以广泛的先占权换取有限的监管收益并削弱关键安全条款，因而不可接受且令人不安。
absEn: This article critiques a leaked draft AI regulatory bill attributed to Anthropic, arguing that it is unacceptable and troubling. The author contends that the bill is weaker than Anthropic's June framework and offers both forward-looking and backward-looking preemption in exchange for modest gains, despite months of movement toward stronger regulation. While acknowledging some good provisions—broader coverage, movable thresholds, risk reports, annual audits, whistleblower protections, security requirements, and inclusion of automated AI R&D risks—the author questions why these must be traded away and criticizes the removal of FRONTIER's cost-benefit analysis requirement for catastrophic risks, the addition of a 'kill switch' provision, and weakened incident-response obligations. The conclusion is that passing preemption in exchange for as little as possible is the way to 'pass nothing,' and that Anthropic needs to course correct quickly, since what Anthropic would accept is a limiting factor in what can be achieved.
absZh: 本文批评了一份据称由 Anthropic 起草的泄露版人工智能监管法案草案，认为其不可接受且令人不安。作者主张，该法案比 Anthropic 六月份提出的框架更为薄弱，以提供前瞻性和回溯性先占权为代价换取有限收益，尽管此前数月监管一直在朝更严格的方向推进。作者虽然承认其中有一些良好条款——更广的覆盖范围、可调整的门槛、风险报告、年度审计、举报人保护、安全要求，以及将自动化人工智能研发风险纳入其中——但质疑为何必须将这些条款作为交换代价，并批评该草案取消了 FRONTIER 对灾难性风险的成本收益分析要求、新增了“终止开关”条款，以及削弱了事件响应义务。结论是，以尽可能少的代价通过先占权，实际上等于“什么都不通过”；Anthropic 需要迅速纠正方向，因为 Anthropic 愿意接受的内容会限制实际能够达成的监管成果。

limits.en: Analysis based on leaked draft, not final bill; provisions may change.
limits.zh: 分析基于泄露草案而非最终法案，条款可能变化。

limits.en: Author's critique may reflect advocacy bias against industry-friendly regulation.
limits.zh: 作者批评可能反映反对行业友好监管的倡导偏见。

limits.en: Assumes preemption is inherently negative, ignoring potential benefits of uniform federal rules.
limits.zh: 假定先占权本质负面，忽略统一联邦规则潜在益处。

limits.en: Does not quantify costs of weakened incident response or kill switch.
limits.zh: 未量化削弱事件响应或终止开关的成本。

limits.en: Limited discussion of political feasibility and trade-offs in lame duck session.
limits.zh: 对跛脚鸭会议政治可行性与权衡讨论有限。

paras.en: I have not had the time to do so, but the other usual suspects quickly sprinted to RTFB (read the bill) and they did not like what they saw. You can try to call this a 'pretty reasonable AI safety bill' as Charlie Bullock does, but that is by the standards of people trying to protect the industry from more impactful regulation.
paras.zh: 我还没有时间这样做，但其他那些常见的怀疑者迅速跑去 RTFB（读法案），而他们并不喜欢自己所看到的内容。你可以像 Charlie Bullock 那样，称这是一项“相当合理的 AI 安全法案”，但那是按照那些试图保护该行业免受更具影响力监管的人的标准而言的。

paras.en: The new Anthropic bill is weaker than their June framework, and offers both forward-looking and backward-looking preemption in exchange, despite months of movement to enable us to do more. What are we even doing?
paras.zh: 新的 Anthropic 法案比他们六月的框架更弱，并且以提供前瞻性和回溯性优先权作为交换，尽管数月来已有进展使我们能够做更多事情。我们到底在做什么？

paras.en: Well, I know what it looks like Anthropic is prioritizing. The silly mistakes are a known and acceptable hazard, but there are things that really should not have made it into a bill that is being pitched to lawmakers.
paras.zh: 嗯，我知道 Anthropic 看起来在优先考虑什么。那些愚蠢的错误是已知且可接受的隐患，但有些东西确实不应该出现在一份正在向立法者推销的法案中。

full.sec: Not Everything Here Is Bad But Oh Boy

paras.en: As noted above, there are some good individual provisions. I like the broader coverage, that thresholds can move both ways, required risk reports and annual audits. The whistleblower provisions and security requirements seem strong.
paras.zh: 如上所述，有一些好的个别条款。我喜欢更广泛的覆盖范围，阈值可以双向变动，要求风险报告和年度审计。举报人条款和安全要求似乎很强。

paras.en: Putting automated AI R&D into the list of risks is very cool and necessary.
paras.zh: 将自动化 AI 研发列入风险清单非常酷且必要。

paras.en: The question is, even if you wanted to build on the FRONTIER framework, why treat this as a trade where you have to then give up other things?
paras.zh: 问题是，即使你想在 FRONTIER 框架上构建，为什么要将其视为一种交易，然后你必须放弃其他东西？

paras.en: And why are we this deadly afraid of what the White House might do, when they clearly already can take down a model with things like export controls or otherwise order you around? Then we add a ‘kill switch’ provision that seems written mostly out of terror that it might get abused. We also get traditional Anthropic objections like ‘we don’t want to have to respond to safety incidents within 72 hours unless it is a true emergency.’
paras.zh: 为什么我们如此害怕白宫可能做的事情，而他们显然已经可以通过出口管制之类的手段搞垮一个模型，或者以其他方式命令你？然后我们添加了一个‘终止开关’条款，似乎主要是出于对可能被滥用的恐惧而写的。我们还得到了传统的 Anthropic 反对意见，比如‘我们不想在 72 小时内对安全事件做出回应，除非是真正的紧急情况。’

paras.en: Why take out FRONTIER’s requirements for a cost-benefit analysis on catastrophic risks and substitute at best highly weak tea?
paras.zh: 为什么要删除 FRONTIER 对灾难性风险进行成本效益分析的要求，并至少用非常弱的茶来代替？

paras.en: The maximally charitable reading is that doing anything is a tough sell even now, and the White House wants no bill, so you have to give and take, and this is as good as one can hope to do modulo fixing its bugs.
paras.zh: 最善意的解读是：即便在当下，做任何事都很难推动，而白宫不想要法案，所以你不得不有所取舍，而这就是在修复其缺陷之外所能期望的最好结果。

paras.en: Except this is backwards. The way to 'pass nothing' is to pass preemption, in the lame duck, in exchange for as little as possible. If the White House fails to realize this, that does not change facts on the ground.
paras.zh: 只不过这是本末倒置。要“什么都不通过”，办法是在跛脚鸭会期通过优先权条款，以换取尽可能少的让步。如果白宫没有意识到这一点，那也不会改变既成事实。

paras.en: Anthropic needs to course correct, quickly. Earlier yesterday I already expressed, here at the conference I am at, that 'what Anthropic would go for' looks like a limiting factor in what we can achieve. And, well, here we are.
paras.zh: Anthropic 需要迅速纠正方向。昨天早些时候，在我所在的会议上，我已经表达过，“Anthropic 会接受什么”看起来是我们所能达成目标的一个限制因素。而如今，事情就摆在这里。
